newsitem.title: INDIA: India's GAIL 1996/97 net up 20.2 pct.
newsitem.headline: India's GAIL 1996/97 net up 20.2 pct.

text.p: The state-run Gas Authority of India Ltd (GAIL) earned a net profit of 6.20 billion rupees ($173.18 million) in 1996/97 (April-March), up from 5.16 billion in the previous year, the company said on Monday.
The company in a statement its 1996/97 (April-March) sales rose to 45.41 billion rupees from 44.09 billion in the previous year.

Gas sales increased to 16,798 million metric standard cubic metres per day (MMSCMD) from 16,495 MMSCMD and the production of liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) rose to 599,161 million tonnes from 549,563 million tonnes, the company said.
"GAIL ensured the continuous availability of gas, maximum capacity utilisation at plants and strictly adhered to schedules," a company spokesman said.
GAIL had commissioned several new projects during the year, he said.

The company's current projects, totalling more than 40.0 billion rupees, include a petrochemical complex in Etawah district in northern Uttar Pradesh state, LPG plants at Lakwa in the northeastern state of Assam and Usar in the western Maharashtra state.
"The project at Etawah will be commissioned this year," the spokesman said.
The company also expects to complete work on the expansion of a gas pipeline from Vijaypur to Dadri in the current year, he said.
"We were adding 550 km (340 miles) of pipeline to the existing system between Vijaypur and Dadri. That pipeline has been laid and compressors will be installed this year," he said.
"The petrochemical project should be through this year," he added.
GAIL also launched a pilot project for a gas distribution system to provide gas through pipelines to domestic and commercial users in New Delhi.

The company is awaiting final government approval for projects worth 30.0 billion rupees. They include a gas processing plant at Gandhar in western Gujarat state, an LPG plant at Aunaiya in the Uttar Pradesh and the Kandla-Loni LPG pipeline project.
